references.text: Earlier in the Nazirite law, shaving of the head is mentioned in cases of impurity, showing the connection between the hair offering and the Nazirite vow.
Describes the beginning of the ritual when the Nazirite period is completed, where this shaving is part of the concluding ceremony.
The peace offering (זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים) is described in detail here; it is the same offering upon which the hair is placed in Numbers 6:18.
Further provisions concerning the peace offering that supplement the understanding of the ritual in which the Nazirite participates.
Samson was consecrated as a Nazirite, and his hair was tied to his vow, demonstrating the significance of hair in the Nazirite vow.
Samson's hair was shaved off, breaking his Nazirite vow and showing the symbolic meaning of the hair.
Paul participates in a purification ceremony with men who have taken a vow, which likely included shaving the head in accordance with the conclusion of the Nazirite law.
Paul cut his hair at Cenchreae because of a vow, which may be connected to Nazirite practice.
